memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'This is what it means,' Joseph said to him. 'The three branches are three days. Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will put Pharaoh's cup in his hand, just as you used to do when you were his cupbearer.'" - Gen 40:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph interprets the cupbearer's dream, and it is wonderful news: in three days he will be released and fully restored to his old position, once again placing the cup in Pharaoh's hand. God had given the man a picture of his coming deliverance, and through Joseph, He now made its meaning clear. What looked like the end of the cupbearer's story was really about to become a new beginning.

Notice the phrase "Pharaoh will lift up your head." For a prisoner in disgrace, with his head bowed low, this was a promise of dignity restored — of being raised up again. God is a God who lifts up the lowly. As the psalmist says, He is "the One who lifts my head high" (Ps 3:3).

It is worth remembering that this word of hope came in a prison, from the mouth of a fellow prisoner. Sometimes the encouragement we need comes from unexpected places — from those who are suffering alongside us, who point us to what God is about to do.

If you are in a season with your head bowed low, take heart. The God who lifted the cupbearer's head is able to lift yours. Your disgrace is not the final word; God specializes in restoration. Hold on to hope, and let Him remind you that He is the One who raises up the downcast in His time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God can lift up my head from a low place?
2. Where do I need to hold on to hope for restoration?
3. Who might God want to encourage through me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the One who lifts my head high. When I am bowed low, remind me that my disgrace is not the final word. Restore me in Your time, and use me to bring hope to others. Amen.
